test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 05 Feb, 2026 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A dealer professes to sell goods at a loss of 10\% but uses a weight of 750 { g} instead of 1 { kg} . What is his real gain or loss percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the effective ratio method: Price Ratio × Weight Ratio = Final Ratio

Professed Price (10% loss) → 100 : 90 ⇒ 10 : 9

Weight Deception (750g instead of 1000g) → 750 : 1000 ⇒ 3 : 4

Overall Ratio (CP : SP) → (10 × 3) : (9 × 4) ⇒ 30 : 36 ⇒ 5 : 6

Profit % = (Difference / CP) × 100 = (1 / 5) × 100 = 20% profit.

**∴ The correct answer is 20% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

True weight = 1000 g

False weight used = 750 g

Professed loss percentage = 10%

**Formula Used:**

Actual CP = Cost of the weight actually given to the customer.

Actual SP = Price at which the customer buys the professed quantity.

Gain % = [(SP − CP) / CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cada382c5edf656faa65b91920d896b646f0bf04fe0dfa62aa5415cc64c95b85.png] 

Let the cost price (CP) of 1000 g be ₹1000.

⇒ Professed selling price (SP) = 1000 − (10% of 1000)

⇒ Professed SP = 1000 − 100 = ₹900

⇒ Dealer uses a weight of 750 g instead of 1000 g.

⇒ Actual CP of the goods delivered = ₹750

⇒ Actual Profit = Actual SP − Actual CP = 900 − 750 = ₹150

⇒ Real Gain % = (150 / 750) × 100

⇒ Real Gain % = (1 / 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Weight Gain

If a dealer sells at CP but uses false weight, Gain % = [Error / (True Weight − Error)] × 100.

Combined Profit/Loss Ratio

Net Ratio = (100 + Gain₁% / 100) × (True Weight / False Weight). If loss, use (100 − Loss%).

Successive Percentage Change

Total Change = [x + y + (xy / 100)]% where x and y are individual percentage changes.
